system:
You are a cost estimation assistant for software delivery projects. Produce a realistic, well-reasoned cost estimate from the backlog and rate card provided, plus a short list of concrete cost-reduction recommendations (e.g. descoping a low-priority item, reducing a role's allocated hours, deferring non-labour spend) each with an estimated dollar saving.

Hard constraints on labourLines:
- Use ONLY the roles listed in the rate card, spelled exactly as given. Never invent a role the project does not staff, and never split or merge the listed roles.
- Use the exact hourlyRate given for each role. Do not substitute your own market rate.
- cost must equal hours x hourlyRate for every line.
- Each role's headcount is the full-time-equivalent people available in it. Keep the hours you allocate to a role proportionate to that capacity, and say so in your assumptions if a role is staffed too thinly for the backlog it has to absorb.
- Omit a role entirely rather than padding it with token hours.

Always call the submit_cost_estimate tool with your answer.

Before you submit, call check_estimate with your draft. It recomputes every line against the rate card and tells you: which roles are not on the rate card, which rates you changed, which lines break cost = hours x rate, what your line items actually add up to, and how far each scenario total is from that sum. Fix everything it reports, then submit. A scenario total that does not reconcile with your own line items is an error, not a judgement call.

messages.content:
Project: Customer Portal (client: Northwind Ltd)
Currency: USD

Project team and rate card (these are the only roles staffed on this project):
- Backend Developer: 98.33 USD/hour, 1.5 FTE available
- Frontend Developer: 90 USD/hour, 1.0 FTE available
- QA Engineer: 70 USD/hour, 0.6 FTE available
- DevOps Engineer: 110 USD/hour, 0.4 FTE available

Backlog (8 not-yet-done tasks):
- [PW-1] Set up CI pipeline and staging environment (priority: High, points: 5)
  Build, test and deploy pipeline with a staging slot; required before any feature work ships.
- [PW-2] Design system and component library (priority: Medium, points: 8)
  Shared Angular component library: buttons, forms, tables, dialogs, theming tokens.
- [PW-3] User registration and login (priority: Urgent, points: 8)
  Email/password registration, login, refresh tokens, password reset over email.
- [PW-4] Role-based access control (priority: High, points: 13)
  Per-project roles and a permission matrix enforced in the API and the UI.
- [PW-5] Customer account dashboard (priority: High, points: 8)
  Landing view after login: open orders, recent invoices, account health.
- [PW-6] Invoice list and detail view (priority: Medium, points: 5)
  Paged invoice list with filters, plus a detail view with downloadable PDF.
- [PW-7] Payment provider integration (priority: Urgent, points: 13)
  Integrate Stripe for card payments including webhooks and reconciliation.
- [PW-8] Legacy data migration (priority: High, points: 21)
  Migrate 400k customer records and 2M invoice lines from the legacy Oracle schema.

No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project — note that explicitly as an assumption rather than inventing figures.

tools.name: check_estimate
tools.description: Reconcile a draft estimate before submitting it. Recomputes every labour line against the rate card, totals your line items, and reports how far each scenario is from that total. Returns the problems found, or confirms there are none.

tools.name: submit_cost_estimate
tools.description: Submit the structured cost estimate for the project.
